To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the beam emittance blowup due to the RF field can be compensated by using a second RF cavity, and that the emittance blowup can be reduced by a factor of two.

the use of a second RF cavity downstream of a conventional gun can compensate for the first and second-order phase dependences of the transverse emittance, thus enabling the use of higher injection phases, and the extraction of long bunches with higher beam brightness.

the use of an asymmetric RF cavity downstream of the gun can compensate for both the first-order and the second-order phase dependence of the transverse emittance blow-up in the gun, and that the longitudinal emittance of the beam can be minimized at injection phases that maximize the bunch length, allowing the use of longer RF bunches and a higher beam brightness.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a new approach to RF gun emittance correction.

the study of the beam emittance in a gun cavity, and the possibility of correcting it by means of an unsymmetri- cal RF cavity, which is fully uncoupled and can be independently phased with respect to the main gun cavity.
the optimization of RF guns, with the aim of improving the beam brightness of future electron and positron sources.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the use of an RF cavity downstream of the gun, fully decoupled from the gun cavity, allows one to compensate for the emittance blowup induced by the gun cavity, even if the injection phase is far from the optimum one, and to obtain a significant increase of the beam brightness.

the use of a second RF cavity, added to the gun and independently phased, allows one to recover the minimum transverse emittance value at a given injection phase, and to achieve the best possible longitudinal emittance at a given longitudinal phase.
the use of the proposed RF gun configuration is a promising way to improve the beam performance in high brightness electron sources.

, in the presence of a non-optimized injection phase, the emittance increase due to the RF field in the gun is partially compensated by the RF field in a second cavity.
the emittance blowup can be corrected with the addition of an extra RF cavity.
we have shown the existence of a new method for RF guns emittance correction, and that the results of the analytical study are in good agreement with those of the numerical simulations.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the use of an additional, downstream, cavity can be exploited to correct the emittance growth in RF guns, allowing to recover the minimum value of the emittance even at injection phases different from the optimal one.
a significant emittance reduction is obtained, even at high injection phases, with respect to conventional RF guns, where the emittance blowup is very strong.

a significant increase of the beam brightness is expected in the case of a gun with an unsymmetrical downstream cavity, with the possibility of a further improvement by using a second unsymmetrical cavity in series with the previous one.
